name: Theca Steroid-Producing Cell Malignant Tumor of Ovary, Not Further Specified
aliases: Malignant Theca Cell Tumor of Ovary

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Theca Cell Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of malignant theca cells with steroidogenic features on histopathological examination
Positive immunostaining for inhibin, calretinin, and steroidogenic enzymes
Clinical signs of androgen or estrogen excess such as virilization or abnormal uterine bleeding

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant theca cells with positive immunohistochemical markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other ovarian sex cord-stromal tumors and metastatic malignancies.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes hirsutism, deepening of voice, and clitoromegaly
Manifested as abnormal uterine bleeding or postmenopausal bleeding

common.notes: Palpable adnexal mass on physical examination

laboratory: Elevated serum testosterone and estradiol levels
Increased inhibin and anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels
Possible elevated serum calcium in paraneoplastic syndrome
imaging: Ultrasound showing solid adnexal mass with increased vascularity
MRI demonstrating ovarian tumor with heterogeneous enhancement
CT scan for staging and detection of metastases
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; molecular profiling may show steroidogenic enzyme gene alterations
other: Histopathology revealing malignant theca cells with steroidogenic differentiation
Immunohistochemical positivity for inhibin, calretinin, and SF-1

distinguishingFeatures: Granulosa cell tumors typically produce estrogen but rarely androgen excess
Histology shows Call-Exner bodies absent in theca cell tumors
Different immunohistochemical profile with FOXL2 mutation
Androblastomas (Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors) produce androgens but have distinct histology
Presence of Sertoli and Leydig cell components
Different clinical presentation with earlier onset virilization

redFlags: Rapid onset of virilization symptoms in adult female
Presence of large adnexal mass with solid features on imaging
Postmenopausal bleeding associated with ovarian mass
references: Young RH. Sex Cord-Stromal Tumors of the Ovary and Testis: Their Similarities and Differences with Other Tumors. Mod Pathol. 2020.
Orphanet Report on Theca Cell Tumors. Orphanet. 2023.
Kurman RJ, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 5th Edition. IARC. 2020.
